subject: MSA / Order Form addendum: Early-exit fee & notice harmonization
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenwaveanalytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Greenwave Legal <legal@greenwaveanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: MSA + Order Form — Term & Exit for pilot

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Procurement/legal at Greenwave asked me to surface a couple of term points so we can get the pilot order signed without a full MSA cycle. Two items they flagged:

- Auto-renew: The order form shows auto-renew by default for individual orders. For the pilot (3 months), our team is pushing to opt-out of auto-renew or require 90-day prior notice to renew.
- Termination for convenience & early-exit fee: Our counsel says termination for convenience should be allowed but they want clarity on any early-exit charges — they proposed a 2-month service fee as a termination charge if we exit before the pilot completes.

I attached your redline (MSA_v3_redline.docx) with their callouts. Can your legal or sales ops propose a short addendum we can sign to capture pilot-specific mechanics so Procurement can approve? We want something lightweight — not a new SOW.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight cadence.

Best,
Asha

Attachments: MSA_v3_redline.docx (docx)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenwaveanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-14T15:26:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — Term & Exit for pilot

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear summary and the attached callouts.

Quick answer from the sales side: we can do a lightweight pilot addendum instead of reworking the full MSA. Proposed commercial compromise from my side:

- For pilot orders (<= 3 months) we remove automatic renewal; the order will expire at term unless both parties opt into renewal.
- If Greenwave wants to be able to terminate for convenience during the pilot but avoid a large hit, we could accept a small early-exit fee — I will confirm the cap with legal, but thinking 1x the monthly committed spend is reasonable.

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in to propose precise contract language and confirm whether 1x monthly cap and no-auto-renew for pilot is workable from a risk and ops perspective.

Asha — if you like this approach I can draft a 1-page addendum (Pilot Addendum draft) for signatures.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pilot_addendum_draft.docx (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@greenwaveanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — Term & Exit for pilot

Markus / Karthik / Asha — thanks, looped in from legal.

We can do a short addendum. Below are the recommended terms (redline attached) that balance Greenwave's procurement ask and Redwood's operational considerations:

1) Pilot orders ("Pilot") defined as orders with term <= 3 months.
2) Auto-renew: Pilot orders will NOT auto-renew. Order will expire at the end of the Pilot unless both parties execute a new order or agree to extend in writing at least 60 days prior to expiration.
3) Termination for convenience during Pilot: Either party may terminate the Pilot with 60 days' prior written notice. If Customer terminates for convenience before the end of the Pilot, Customer will pay an early-exit fee equal to the lesser of (a) one (1) month of the Customer's then-committed monthly spend under the Order Form, or (b) the remaining prepaid/committed amount; Redwood will pro-rate any prepaid amounts for unused service days and provide a credit for unused committed spend.
4) SOW / Order alignment: Any extension beyond Pilot shall be documented via a new Order Form; pricing for a post-pilot committed term will be negotiated separately.

Suggested language snippet for addendum (for your draft):
"For Pilot Orders (defined as Orders with a term of three months or less), the Parties agree that the Order will not automatically renew. Either Party may terminate a Pilot Order for convenience with sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Customer elects to terminate a Pilot Order for convenience prior to the end of the Pilot term, Customer shall pay Redwood an early-exit fee not to exceed the lesser of (i) one (1) month of Customer's then-current committed monthly spend or (ii) the remaining pre-paid amount under the Order; Redwood shall credit Customer for any unused prepaid portions of the Order on a pro rata basis"

Rationale: 60-day notice gives Procurement a predictable window but avoids an excessive multi-month termination charge that blocks pilots. The cap at 1x monthly spend is consistent with our existing pilot concessions and keeps ops refundable.

I attached MSA_section_2_term_redline.docx with the exact addendum draft for signatures.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_section_2_term_redline.docx (docx)

Date: 2026-06-16T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — Term & Exit for pilot

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the pragmatic language. Procurement is generally comfortable with removing auto-renew for a pilot and the 60-day notice. A couple of notes from our side:

- Our counsel still prefers an early-exit fee equal to two (2) months' committed spend to cover ramp costs. They will need to see the final addendum to sign off.
- Procurement asked whether Redwood can credit any unused committed tokens / prepayments back to Greenwave (good to hear you included a pro-rata credit).

I'm attaching our approval matrix to show internal routing timelines — if we can get final redline by Friday we can route it through Legal + Procurement next week.

Asha — thanks for the note and for sharing the approval matrix. Good news: we can accept the 60-day non-renew/termination notice plus the pro-rata credit for unused prepaid amounts. On the early-exit fee we are willing to cap at one (1) month of committed spend (not two), but to make Procurement comfortable we will add a short explanation clause in the addendum that the cap is intended to cover reasonable ramp costs and that Redwood will not seek additional liquidated damages beyond the cap.

Next steps:
- Marissa: please finalize the one-page Pilot Addendum using the snippet you provided and include the explanatory clause re: ramp costs.
- Asha: if Procurement/Law approves the 1x cap, I will send the final addendum via DocuSign for signature.

If we can close by early next week we will get the pilot started the following Monday.

Thanks,
Markus
